newsitem.title: ROMANIA: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 1 PM.
newsitem.headline: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 1 PM.

text.p: * The Central Electoral Bureau (BEC) released partial results in November 3 parliament and presidential elections from 99.35 percent of polling stations, saying some 90 stations in Bucharest were still expected to submit their vote count.
Results put President Ion Iliescu ahead with 32.3 percent, followed by Emil Constantinescu with 28.07 percent and Petre Roman with 20.5 percent.

The opposition Democratic Convention (CDR) bloc leads in both parliament houses with 30.5 percent in the Senate and 30.01 percent in the lower Chamber of Deputies. Ruling Party of Social Democracy (PDSR) comes second with 23.1 percent, respectively 21.6 percent.
The third political group in parliament is the Social Democratic Union (USD) who got 13.17 percent of votes in the Senate and 12.9 percent in the lower house.
* The foreign ministry has coordinated voting procedures in 97 countries outside Romania, with a total turnout of 39,000, the ministry spokesman Sorin Ducaru told reporters.
Ducaru said accreditations for foreign observers and journalists are valid for the run-off to presidential polls.
* Despite irregularities, the November 3 polls were well organised, state secretary Adrian Duta said.

* Technical irregularities did not influence the results of Sunday polls, said Marian Tata, leader of the human rights group Pro Democratia which had some 3,000 observers in the parliament and presidential elections.
* Romanian President Ion Iliescu, PDSR's candidate for a new term, hailed the high turnout of Sunday polls, saying Romanians have proven their political maturity.
* Iliescu called for a political accord to ensure continuity of reforms and integration in the European Union and NATO as well as a social pact to foster restructuring and social protection.
* Iliescu said the CDR has won elections due to generous promises which are hard to keep, while voters sanctioned PDSR's unpopular measures during transition.
He acknowledged some errors made by the government in the past years.
* Former Hungarian Foreign Minister Geza Jeszenszky told a news conference he was confident the Hungarian Democratic Union will be part of ruling coalition after elections.

* Foreign ministry state secretary Lazar Comanescu to hand on November 8 President Iliescu's message to Iceland's President Olafur Ragnar Grimsson pleading for support in Romania's efforts to join NATO in a first wave of expansion.
A similar message will be delievered on Thursday by defence state secretary Mircea Pascu to Portuguese president Jorge Sampaio. -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
